subject: penguins
one_liner: The dating app where female penguins make the first move, because the colony has 40,000 visually identical males and someone has to be decisive.
brand_voice_notes: Bumble's empowerment register applied to seabirds with total sincerity. HR-approved courtship. Everything is a workflow with an SLA. The app never acknowledges that penguins cannot read, hold devices, or agree to terms of service. Urgency is a feature: every match expires in 24 hours, which the company presents as respect for her time.

hero.sub: Rookery gives female penguins the confidence to choose between 40,000 visually identical males. Escrowed pebbles, notarized contact calls, and a 24-hour window to make the first move before the match expires with the ice shelf.

features.title: Pebble Escrow
features.blurb: Courtship pebbles are held by a neutral third-party skua until both parties commit to the nest. If he ghosts, you keep the pebbles. Gravel is detected at intake and returned to sender with a formal note.

features.title: Vocal ID
features.blurb: Upload one contact call. We fingerprint the waveform, notarize it, and surface you to males within earshot. Replaces the legacy discovery system, which was shouting.

features.title: Molt Mode
features.blurb: Your profile auto-hides for the duration of your catastrophic molt. You return to the queue in three weeks, fully waterproof, with your match rate and escrow balance intact.

demo_screen_concept: The first-move inbox: a queue of matched male penguins rendered as portrait cards that are visually identical on purpose, distinguished only by metadata (pebble portfolio grade, call quality score, distance in floes). Each card wears a 24-hour countdown ring that expires the match. Selecting a match opens the approved-opener drawer with three notarized contact calls to choose from. A sidebar shows the pebble escrow balance and a skua arbitration status feed. Filters along the top: distance in floes, molt status, pebble grade.

images.rationale: 16:9 hero skipped: the sticker-poster hero wants a square ringed portrait, so the hero slot became a 1:1 female portrait inside the countdown ring. Demo is photo-shaped (dating profile cards): one male portrait generated and deliberately reused on every demo card, because the males are visually identical and that is the joke. Two testimonial headshots (Marguerite, Deb); Sandra P. keeps the CSS initials treatment to stay in budget.

design_direction.style: Sticker-sheet consumer poster, glacier daylight mode. The page is staged as the consumer site of a heavily funded female-first dating company that has decided the Antarctic breeding colony is an underserved market and files courtship under decision support. A cold glacier-white ground (#F5F9FB) runs the whole page with no gradients and no texture; structure comes from chunky poster blocks: flat white and yolk-yellow panels with 2px penguin-ink borders, 16px radii, and a single hard 6px offset ink shadow with zero blur, so every card sits on the page like a die-cut sticker peeled from a sheet. No glass, no blur, no clay shadow pairs, no hairline editorial rules. The core motif is the countdown ring: a thick ink-stroked circular timer, always drawn mid-expiry, that wraps profile portraits, tier badges, and the hero mark, because on Rookery every match dies in 24 hours and the company considers urgency a form of respect. The second motif is the pebble: a smooth grey speckled SVG oval used as currency chip, list bullet, escrow badge, and rating unit, with certified pebbles wearing a small ink checkmark and rejected gravel stamped GRAVEL in mono caps. One brood-yolk yellow (#FFC116) carries the wordmark block, every primary CTA, the highlighted word per headline, and the sticker panels behind key numbers; one rationed ice-water blue (#1C7FA6) is reserved strictly for verified states and live escrow telemetry (the skua arbitration feed, notarization checkmarks, the live colony dot) and appears nowhere else. Nunito sets the wordmark and headlines in rounded ExtraBlack caps with app-store confidence; DM Sans carries plain, faintly HR-handbook body copy. Every figure that pretends to be colony telemetry (countdown clocks, pebble balances, match-rate percentages, tier prices) is set in Spline Sans Mono with tabular figures inside ink-bordered white wells, so it reads like the escrow ledger, not marketing. Motion is sticker-restrained: countdown rings sweep once on load then hold, cards lift 2px on hover with the offset shadow deepening to 8px, pebbles wobble once on first reveal, CTAs depress 1px on press with the shadow collapsing to 2px, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur panels, no neon glow, no clay, no bento lattice, no didone engraving, no condensed athletic type, no HUD brackets, no nautical chrome, no storefront capsules, no emoji. Reads like a company that files pair bonding under 'decision support' and considers the male penguin an inventory problem.

design_direction.archetype: Female-first consumer dating app staged as a sticker-bright poster site: split hero with a countdown-ringed portrait and monumental rounded headline, three die-cut feature stickers, testimonial cards with ringed headshots, pricing as a three-sticker ladder, closing CTA band, handoff to the first-move inbox demo.

design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero on glacier white: left, monumental Nunito ExtraBlack headline with 'first' on a yolk sticker block, HR-handbook subcopy, yolk CTA with hard ink shadow; right, a single female penguin portrait inside a thick countdown ring at 70% expiry, wearing a VERIFIED WADDLE badge in ice blue, with two pebble chips and a 24:00:00 mono timer stickered on the ring's edge.
